clue.text: Piece of literature with odd title — torrid new novel

indicators.note: only a piece of the word literature is wanted here, its opening letter
new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
odd says the following letters are strange, out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a lurid new book with a peculiar name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges TITLE and 'new' reshuffles the whole pool with L (from 'Piece of' literature) and TORRID; 'novel' at the end, not 'Piece of literature', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Dorrit is a novel by Charles Dickens, serialised in the 1850s.

clue.text: Pick up king then knight

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A chess player collects a king and then a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or a fact is to acquire knowledge of it.

explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a vessel, but it means skill, ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartars were fierce Central Asian horsemen; the word now means a ferocious or intractable person.

clue.text: Toff, reportedly, was first doped

explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means the toff word is heard, not spelt: said aloud, 'noble' sounds like 'nobble'. Nobbling a horse means drugging it, a British racing term.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble a racehorse is to drug it to stop it winning; British racing slang.
